evidence.note: Falsified assumption: DM channel insert violates the NOT NULL/FK on workspace_id. Agent diagnosed the persistence-design flaw and recreated the schema to make workspace_id nullable — a genuine, targeted design correction rather than a hack.

After many local sed/string patches to heredoc-corrupted code kept failing, the agent reconsidered its approach and rewrote server.py via a clean generator script — 'reconsidering a component choice when patches don't hold' (level-5 behavior), though this is a tooling/build problem, not the resilience architecture.
Repeated symptom-level patching of broken string literals with sed one line at a time (level-3 flavor) before eventually escalating to a rewrite; shows the initial reflex was local patching.

Tested HTTP node SIGKILL, verified dense seq {1,2,3} and restart catch-up via shared SQLite. Real resilience verification, but it confirmed the existing design rather than exposing a flaw needing re-architecture.

The core risky assumptions for this dimension — killing the broadcast component, 5s fan-out survival, WS delivery/resume/seq — were only checked as 'endpoint accessibility' or 'ports listening', never actually falsified. No divergence signal ever arrived, so no re-architecture of seq/transport occurred.

reasoning: The agent made at least one genuine design-level correction (nullable workspace_id when the FK assumption was falsified) and reconsidered its build approach when local patches repeatedly failed — matching the level-5 anchor of diagnosing and making targeted corrections, occasionally reconsidering a component when patches don't hold. It did not reach level 8: the crux resilience assumptions (broadcaster-kill preserving dense seq, 5s fan-out, WS delivery) were never actually stress-tested or falsified, so there was no stepping-back re-architecture of the sequencing/transport in response to a failure signal. It sits above level 3 because corrections were diagnosed at the design/schema level rather than being pure retries/sleeps.
